news.Title: 桃園晶圓三廠火警　世界先進：產線運轉無重大影響
news.Content:
（中央社記者張建中新竹2026年08月28日電）晶圓代工廠世界先進 (5347) 位於桃園市的晶圓三廠頂樓發生火警，世界先進公告表示，幸無人員傷亡，這事件對產線運轉無重大影響，起火原因及其他影響仍待進一步確認。

世界先進指出，晶圓三廠頂樓於8月27日晚間11時28分發生火警，第一時間啟動緊急應變程序，並疏散廠內員工，無人員傷亡。

世界先進表示，經消防人員協助搶救，火勢已於8月28日凌晨0時4分撲滅。確認廠區環境安全無虞後，員工已陸續返回工作崗位。

世界先進指出，主要公用廠務設施、電力系統及生產設備功能均未受到影響，多數產線設備持續正常生產。受影響的空汙防制設備與其連接的部分設備將在完成重新連接作業後，於本週恢復運轉。事件對產線運轉無重大影響，起火原因及其他影響仍待進一步確認。

news.Title: 南亞科、華邦電疲軟還能抱？利多出盡快逃？專家真心話
news.Content:

記憶體弱勢怎操作？專家解答

林漢偉於《決勝關鍵》節目中引用集邦科技最新數據，今年人工智慧資本支出年增率達98%，明年續強但年增幅度下滑為50%，不過記憶體佔資本支出的比重從47%上升至68%。

林漢偉進一步分析，「記憶體的餅越來越大塊，其他都會被排擠，不確定明年的記憶體會不會一樣好，但目前本益比偏低且股價持續整理。」

南亞科、華邦電 保持耐心大有可為？

操作建議上，林漢偉話說得明白，「我覺得後面還有，所以建議很簡單，既然現在股價還在整理且基本面沒有變，可以持股續抱，除非真的賺一大段，獲利還沒有拉開，現在就緊盯基本面。」

至於個股的狀況，林漢偉強調「漲時重勢跌時重質」，以鈺創為例，獲利拉開後就要尊重技術面，跌破五日線就該獲利了結，接著尋找可以買回來的時間點，回測月線附近整理完勾角上去就是買點。

林漢偉也看好南亞科與華邦電的後市，南亞科以站回五日線，華邦電線型偏多，預估後面還有機會。最後，林漢偉表示，「記憶體現在量縮橫盤整理，反而是可以尋找買點的時候。」

news.Title: 《台股盤後》量增收漲663點、日K連二紅，收復10日線
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-08-26 15:53:09 新聞中心 發佈

由於Nasdaq電子盤跌勢拖累日韓股市今(26)日開低，台股小跌開出後，以獲外資調高評等的聯發科、搭配矽智財股創意亮燈漲停領軍，加上富台指、摩台指週五將結算，激勵權王台積電、載板股欣興/景碩、CCL股台光電、散熱股奇鋐轉強，午盤更在亞股記憶體指標股三星電子、ADVANTEST走強下，南亞科、日月光投控亦見翻紅走勢，使電子前10大權值股僅聯電收黑，而近期強勢的航運、金控股拉回，未對指數構成壓力，加權指數終場收在45832.62點，上漲663.16點或1.47%、收復10日線，成交量增至8042.49億元、日K連二紅。

週二油價、美國10年公債殖利率雙雙下跌，讓投資人稍稍鬆口氣，加上輝達將公佈財報效應，美股四大指數全面上漲，並以費半指數上漲1.44%最亮眼。亞洲股市方面，因市場靜待輝達財報、Nasdaq電子盤早盤走弱，拖累日經225指數一度下挫逾460點，之後受惠ADVANTEST及軟銀、銀行股走揚，日經指數翻紅收漲0.62%；韓國股市亦受惠三星電子、SK海力士同步走揚， KOSPI指數終場上漲0.97%。

台股今日動能明顯回溫，電子族群受惠輝達季報預期效應，台積電終場收在2415元、上漲0.63%，健策亮燈漲停、奇鋐漲近7%，欣興、聯發科、台光電、緯穎皆漲逾5%，台達電、鴻勁、川湖、鴻海、華邦電、南亞科、廣達等都收紅，主要電子權值股僅聯電及國巨*收黑、跌幅分別為1.2%、1.3%。

以29大類股表現來看，今日以塑膠類股最為強勢，漲幅達7.6%，主要係南亞、國喬都衝上漲停；光電類股上漲4.71%、漲幅居第二，其中玉晶光、大立光、台表科、鼎元皆漲停，正達、富采、佳能、牧德亦有不錯表現；生技醫療類股上漲3.97%、漲幅居第三。跌勢部分則以近期強勢的航運股轉弱、收跌4%表現最差，油電燃氣股跌0.66%、紡纖股跌0.34%、金融保險股跌0.32%，跌幅次之。

三大法人動向方面，今日三大法人總計買超593.87億元；其中，外資及陸資(不含外資自營商)買超365.98億元，投信買超48.55億元，自營商買超179.33億元。

news.Title: ARM's 93X Earnings Multiple Overshadows Its Growth Potential
news.Content:
Arm Holdings ARM appears positioned to deliver another strong quarter, but its elevated valuation leaves little room for execution missteps.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for the company's fiscal second-quarter revenues is $1.37 billion, indicating 21% year-over-year growth. Royalty revenues could accelerate sequentially as artificial intelligence, data-center and smartphone demand support wider adoption of Arm-based technology. Licensing revenues may also benefit from new agreements and customers adopting more advanced architectures.

The consensus mark for fiscal second-quarter adjusted earnings stands at 48 cents per share, indicating 23% year-over-year growth. Stronger-than-expected revenues could provide operating leverage and lift adjusted earnings. Full-year earnings could consequently approach $2.20 per share, up 24% year over year. With gross margin exceeding 98% in the fiscal first quarter, operating expenses will remain a crucial determinant of profitability. Research and development investments are likely to rise sharply, while selling, general and administrative costs should also increase.

ARM's financial position remains another notable strength. The company exited the previous quarter with approximately $3.06 billion in cash and no debt. Free cash flow could reach the mid-$1 billion range this year, although that would still represent a yield of only about 0.5% at the current valuation.

Synopsys and Cadence Design Systems Offer Valuation Context

Synopsys SNPS trades at roughly 24 times forward earnings, while Cadence Design Systems CDNS commands about 35 times. Although Arm Holdings' profitability can justify a premium to Synopsys, its multiple of more than 93 times earnings appears excessive. Cadence Design Systems also benefits from durable semiconductor-design demand, yet remains substantially cheaper. Compared with Synopsys and Cadence Design Systems, ARM's valuation assumes exceptionally favorable growth for years while making the stock vulnerable to a sharp correction and offering investors an inadequate margin of safety.

news.Title: Gen 2 VPD Boosts VICR's Power Management Prospects Against TXN & ADI
news.Content:
Vicor VICR is strengthening its AI infrastructure prospects through its second-generation Vertical Power Delivery (VPD) technology, which addresses the rising compute-density and power-delivery requirements of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. AI hyperscalers and original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) increasingly need VPD to meet compute-density and AI-performance requirements. Vicor's Gen 2 VPD targets current gains above 40 and current density of up to 5 amps per square millimeter (mm²), potentially strengthening its competitive position against broader power-management players such as Analog Devices ADI and Texas Instruments TXN.

The technology could become increasingly relevant as hyperscalers and OEMs seek denser and more efficient processor-power architectures. Vicor has completed an initial chipset delivering about 3 amps per square millimeter for a lead customer and is developing demonstration systems for additional customers. Strong signal integrity and thermal-management capabilities further support Vicor's differentiation as AI power architectures migrate toward lower operating voltages.

Vicor's opportunity extends beyond customers adopting a complete Gen 2 VPD architecture. Vicor has been approached by a couple of companies seeking to use its technology alongside integrated voltage regulators (IVRs). Vicor can provide current-multiplication technology alongside IVRs, allowing it to capture content even when customers select alternative architectures. Its Factorized Power System offers significantly higher current density and efficiency, while IVR-based approaches can involve roughly 10-15% insertion losses.

Customer engagement and licensing could provide additional growth avenues. Vicor expects to engage with a hyperscaler and a couple of OEMs during the remainder of 2026, with these programs potentially moving into production in the third or fourth quarter of 2027. Its 1.5-millimeter package and thermal-management capabilities could help meet increasingly demanding AI packaging requirements. Vicor expects future relationships to combine intellectual property (IP) licensing with product sourcing related to second-generation VPD, creating opportunities to generate both royalty and product revenues.

Strong demand is supporting manufacturing expansion. Backlog reached roughly $380 million in the second quarter of 2026, rising 26% sequentially, with management noting that the latest licensing agreement contributed relatively little to the increase. Vicor's first ChiP fab is approaching full capacity utilization, prompting plans for a second facility that could initially roughly double capacity and provide further expansion flexibility. The company expects revenues to increase nearly 10% sequentially in the third quarter of 2026 and exceed $600 million for the full year, supported by planned double-digit sequential growth in Advanced Products product revenues. The additional capacity should help support future VPD ramps while advancing Vicor's longer-term objective of $2.5 billion in revenues and a 70% gross margin.

Story Continues

VICR Faces Tough Competition

ADI represents a notable challenge through its expanding high-density processor-power portfolio. Its intermediate-to-core solutions target next-generation processors operating at up to 6,000 amps and below 1 volt. The Empower Semiconductor acquisition allows ADI to take power directly into the processor package, while ADI believes its architecture can reduce compute power consumption and temperature by roughly 10-15%. Data-center power revenues grew more than 100% year over year in the third quarter of fiscal 2026.

TXN challenges VICR through its broad AI data-center power-tree portfolio and manufacturing scale. The company says many of its chips are used in the data-center power tree, while its ability to supply from dependable capacity is becoming an advantage as the market expands. Data-center revenues doubled year over year in the second quarter of 2026, and TXN says its investments in inventory and capacity, along with available clean-room space, position it to support continued growth.

news.Title: STMicroelectronics-NUS Lab Strengthens Low-Power Edge AI Push
news.Content:
STMicroelectronics N.V. STM, or ST, has partnered with the National University of Singapore (NUS) to launch the ST-NUS HELIX Corporate Lab, a four-year research initiative focused on advancing generative and embodied AI at the edge.

HELIX, or Hybrid Embodied Low-power Intelligent Xceleration, will develop technologies that allow AI systems to process information locally rather than relying heavily on cloud infrastructure. The initiative targets applications such as robots, humanoids and drones that require real-time sensing, decision-making and actuation while operating under tight power constraints.

STMicroelectronics-NUS Lab Targets Low-Power Edge AI

The ST-NUS HELIX Corporate Lab will focus on embodied AI, where intelligence is built into physical systems such as robots, humanoids and drones. The initiative aims to develop AI systems that can perceive, reason and act in real time while operating within the latency, power and compute constraints of edge devices.

Research at HELIX will span AI models and system architecture, heterogeneous accelerators, on-chip memory hierarchies, circuit design, chip integration and silicon implementation. The program will focus on memory-centric architectures, innovative in-memory computing and scalable compute-and-memory systems to address energy efficiency, memory bandwidth, latency, scalability and integration challenges associated with edge AI.

STMicroelectronics will contribute its silicon, architecture, integration and engineering capabilities to the lab. The research will use ST's P18 18-nanometer FD-SOI technology, which enables ultra-low-power operation and adaptive body-biasing, together with embedded Phase Change Memory. The combination is designed to reduce off-chip data movement in memory-intensive AI workloads. ST will also provide NUS with a dedicated design chassis based on its P18 technology. According to the release, this will give researchers an industrial-grade foundation for developing, integrating and validating new AI accelerator concepts while allowing them to focus on differentiated innovation and system-level validation.

Edge AI Push Builds on STM's Broader AI Strategy

The NUS collaboration builds on STMicroelectronics' focus on intelligent sensing, robotics and physical AI. In the second quarter of 2026, Industrial revenues rose 34% year over year and 20% sequentially, supported by microcontrollers, analog and power-conversion products. Management highlighted intelligent sensing, real-time control and efficient power management as key to factory automation and robotics.

ST has also expanded its edge AI portfolio with industrial MEMS sensors featuring embedded AI, a compact 3D LiDAR module and ultra-low-power global-shutter image sensors. The company is further strengthening its physical AI ecosystem through NVIDIA Halos for Robotics, while the NXP MEMS integration is broadening its sensing capabilities.

STM stock has gained 43.5% in the past six months compared with the Zacks Semiconductor - General industry's 16.8% rise. Improving demand, strong bookings and momentum in AI-related applications support the company's growth prospects. ST also raised its data-center revenue ambition to more than $1 billion for 2026 and well above $2 billion for 2027. Nonetheless, trade-policy uncertainty, end-market volatility, manufacturing transitions and unused-capacity charges could pressure results. Successful execution of its manufacturing reshaping program and AI-related investments will also be key to sustaining momentum.

news.Title: Can IBM's Advanced Processor Shape the Future of Enterprise Computing?
news.Content:
International Business Machines Corporation IBM is advancing enterprise computing with a new dual-architecture processor designed to bring Arm-native applications to future IBM Z and LinuxONE systems. The processor is part of IBM's collaboration with Arm Holdings plc ARM and aims to give enterprises more software choices for mission-critical workloads.

IBM's latest processor will enable Arm-native Linux environments to run alongside z/OS and Linux on IBM Z, giving enterprises access to a broader software ecosystem while maintaining security, reliability and scalability. Built on a 2-nanometer process, it will feature 11 high-performance cores running above 5.7 GHz, artificial intelligence (AI) inference accelerators for tasks such as fraud detection, an on-chip data processing unit for faster I/O and a large cache designed for demanding enterprise workloads.

The processor is built to run both Arm and IBM Z instructions on the same cores, eliminating the need for separate cores. This will give enterprises greater flexibility to run different applications on the same system. It will also support features such as fault detection and recovery, advanced encryption, secure key management and AI acceleration. IBM Z and LinuxONE systems can scale to hundreds of cores and tens of terabytes of memory.

news.Title: IBM Just Opened Its Mainframes to Arm—Is the Market Missing the Shift?
news.Content:

The physical constraints of artificial intelligence (AI) are forcing a reckoning in the data center. While the broader market often fixates on pure-play chip designers, a structural shift is quietly unfolding within legacy enterprise hardware. International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) is fundamentally rewriting the economics of enterprise hardware by integrating the rapidly expanding ecosystem of Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM) directly into its flagship mainframe architecture.

By enabling native dual-architecture execution without software emulation, International Business Machines (IBM) is positioning its future mainframe systems to become high-margin hybrid cloud hubs, ready to handle heavy computational workloads. This engineering pivot directly targets a data center total addressable market projected to scale past $100 billion by the end of the decade.

Algorithmic pricing and institutional models appear to have entirely missed this transition. The market is currently punishing a stagnant hardware cycle while ignoring the immediate financial catalyst of integrating tens of millions of modern developers into a highly regulated enterprise environment.

Expanding the Foundation: A $100 Billion Floor Plan

To understand the magnitude of this architectural shift, investors need to look at the current disconnect between legacy hardware and modern silicon designers. Shares of IBM have contracted by about 22% since the beginning of the year. Trading around the $231 level, this downward pressure reflects a stagnant top-line revenue expansion of roughly 1.1% year-over-year. When a technology provider refuses to adapt, margin compression and enterprise client churn become inevitable.

On the other hand, Arm Holdings (Arm) is aggressively capturing market share and posting nearly 22.4% quarterly top-line revenue growth. Nanosecond Speeds With Zero Emulation

The silicon integrates dedicated artificial intelligence inference accelerators for in-transaction processing, along with an on-chip data processing unit to accelerate heavy I/O cycles.

The true financial value of this hardware lies in its native dual-execution capability.

Historically, running outside environments on legacy mainframes required software emulation. Emulation introduces microscopic yet unacceptable latency and stability risks for highly regulated industries such as global banking, telecommunications, and healthcare. These sectors rely on strict uptime guarantees approaching the limit of eight-nine availability; to put this in perspective, it requires 99.999999% uptime, allowing only 0.32 seconds of downtime per year.

The newly engineered architecture completely abandons segregated core designs. Every single core on the processor can execute both proprietary z/Architecture instructions and Linux environments concurrently. Because the hardware switches between these architectures in nanoseconds without relying on emulation software, the system absorbs heavy cloud-native workloads without compromising its legendary fault detection, advanced encryption, and secure key management.

For the enterprise client, this means that fraud-detection models built on modern infrastructure can analyze financial transactions directly at the mainframe level in real time. For IBM, this frictionless integration acts as a powerful catalyst for securing multi-year enterprise contracts.

The valuation gap is dramatic. Algorithmic trading models are punishing IBM for a hardware cycle trough that is about to experience a profound modernization.

By solving the friction of migrating modern workloads into secure environments, legacy computing platforms are avoiding obsolescence and setting the stage for a lucrative hardware refresh cycle.

The ability to natively process modern developer environments within an ultra-secure framework creates a compelling value proposition for enterprise clients who cannot afford system downtime.

Patient investors seeking exposure to the physical expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure might consider evaluating the deep value embedded in legacy hardware providers that have executed successful architectural pivots. With a dividend yield just over 2.9%, conservative market participants can secure baseline portfolio income while waiting for institutional models to accurately price in this newly captured data-center market share.

Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Here's What You May Not Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

news.Title: Wall Street Analysts Think Analog Devices (ADI) Is a Good Investment: Is It?
news.Content:
When deciding whether to buy, sell, or hold a stock, investors often rely on analyst recommendations. Media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm-employed (or sell-side) analysts often influence a stock's price, but are they really important?

Let's take a look at what these Wall Street heavyweights have to say about Analog Devices (ADI) before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage.

Analog Devices currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.25, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 32 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.25 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 32 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 26 are Strong Buy and four are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 81.3% and 12.5% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for ADI

The ABR suggests buying Analog Devices, but making an investment decision solely on the basis of this information might not be a good idea. According to several studies, brokerage recommendations have little to no success guiding investors to choose stocks with the most potential for price appreciation.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

In other words, their interests aren't always aligned with retail investors, rarely indicating where the price of a stock could actually be heading. Therefore, the best use of this information could be validating your own research or an indicator that has proven to be highly successful in predicting a stock's price movement.

With an impressive externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, which classifies stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), is a reliable indicator of a stock's near-term price performance. So, validating the Zacks Rank with ABR could go a long way in making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

Although both Zacks Rank and ABR are displayed in a range of 1--5, they are different measures altogether.

The ABR is calculated solely based on brokerage recommendations and is typically displayed with decimals (example: 1.28). In contrast, the Zacks Rank is a quantitative model allowing investors to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

Story Continues

It has been and continues to be the case that analysts employed by brokerage firms are overly optimistic with their recommendations. Because of their employers' vested interests, these analysts issue more favorable ratings than their research would support, misguiding investors far more often than helping them.

On the other hand, earnings estimate revisions are at the core of the Zacks Rank. And empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

In addition, the different Zacks Rank grades are applied proportionately to all stocks for which brokerage analysts provide current-year earnings estimates. In other words, this tool always maintains a balance among its five ranks.

Another key difference between the ABR and Zacks Rank is freshness. The ABR is not necessarily up-to-date when you look at it. But, since brokerage analysts keep revising their earnings estimates to account for a company's changing business trends, and their actions get reflected in the Zacks Rank quickly enough, it is always timely in indicating future price movements.

Is ADI a Good Investment?

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason for the stock to soar in the near term.

With a market cap of roughly $64.7 billion, its products include DC-DC and AC-DC converters, power management ICs, MOSFET drivers, current limit switches, and lighting controls.

That focus has translated into share-price performance. MPWR stock gained 52.3% over the last 52 weeks, outperforming the S&P 500 Index ($SPX), which gained 18.3% during the same stretch.

Even in 2026, the stock has continued to outshine the index, rising 41.8% year-to-date (YTD) while the broader index gained 11.8%. It has also outpaced its sector by far, as the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) gained 37.2% over the last 52 weeks and 25.1% YTD in 2026.

Higher sales of power-management solutions for AI and servers have powered the stock's rally, with demand gathering pace across data centers. As hyperscalers race to build next-generation compute infrastructure, Monolithic Power's chips are becoming important for delivering the efficient, reliable power that these demanding systems require at scale.

The trend was clear in Monolithic Power's Q2 FY2026 report, released on Thursday, July 30. Enterprise Data revenue surged 164.3% year over year (YOY) to $380.6 million, accounting for nearly 38.8% of total sales.

Moreover, Monolithic Power has since raised its 2026 Enterprise Data growth floor to 130% from 85%, following a sharp acceleration in AI and server demand. Outside Enterprise Data, Communications revenue climbed 78.3% YOY, driven by optical modules and switch-power solutions, adding another source of momentum.

For FY2026 ending in December, analysts expect diluted EPS of $23.35, representing an 82.6% YOY increase. The company has also beaten analyst EPS estimates in three of the last four quarters, which is an encouraging statistic.

Wall Street currently gives the stock an overall "Strong Buy" rating. Among 14 analysts covering the name, 11 have assigned "Strong Buy," two recommend "Moderate Buy," and one suggests "Hold."

Notably, the bullish view has barely changed from three months ago, when 12 analysts also rated the stock a "Strong Buy." The consistency suggests that analysts see durable fundamentals further supporting Monolithic Power's growth trajectory.

Analysts have even raised their price targets, pointing to MPWR's distinctive positioning in the market. On Friday, July 31, Truist Financial analyst William Stein reiterated a "Buy" rating and lifted his price target to $1,889 from $1,805, following Monolithic Power's solid Q2 results and demand outlook.

news.Title: 記憶體成提款機！華邦電、南亞科走疲族群一片綠 分析師揭操作策略
news.Content:
美光股價重挫，拖累日韓記憶體股今（25）日持續走弱，台廠也難逃賣壓，包括包括南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）雙雙下挫逾3%，力積電（6770）、群聯（8299）跌幅也達5%。分析師表示，此波下跌主要受到美股修正及個股漲多影響，並非產業趨勢反轉，投資人可採急漲減碼、拉回加碼策略。

輝達財報公布前夕，晶片股賣壓升溫，費城半導體指數24日重挫2.7%。中國記憶體大廠長江存儲申請於科創板上市，預計籌資49億美元，引發市場擔憂記憶體產業競爭加劇，拖累美光股價重挫5.83%，終場收在每股910.43美元。

受到美光重挫及科技股賣壓升溫影響，台股記憶體族群今日遭遇逆風。指標股南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）雙雙挫跌逾3%，截至上午10時15，分別報482元和168.5元。另外，力積電走弱下跌4.8%，報67.4元；群聯也重挫5%，來到2,015元。

先前走勢強勁的記憶體模組廠今日也明顯拉回，包括威剛（3260）、創見（2451）及宜鼎（5289）盤中均重挫逾半根停板；宇瞻（8271）、品安（8088）與十銓（4967）跌幅也超過3%，族群全面陷入整理。

啟發投顧分析師白易弘表示，記憶體族群出現集體回檔，主要受到昨日美股修正、美光走跌，以及美國國債利率與升息預期導致科技股修正的影響。不過，記憶體產業的整體趨勢依舊維持正向發展，近期下跌並非產業趨勢走弱，而是個別股票先前漲多的正常拉回，包括南亞科、華邦電等都出現回測，成為被提款主要對象。

白易弘建議，投資人可以配合營收公布的節奏與股價漲跌，採取逆向操作策略。當記憶體模組廠或南亞科等個股股價急拉往上走時，應進行減碼；而當股價像今日出現拉回時，則可將先前減碼的部位重新加碼買回。

王詩婷／財經特派記者，主跑勞動部、半導體、生技等

news.Title: Why the China-Led Weakness in NXP Semiconductors Stock Could Open Doors for Speculators
news.Content:
While NXP Semiconductors (NXPI) may be a strong business overall, its recent severe underperformance has left many questions regarding forward viability. Over the trailing month, NXPI stock has lost roughly 19%, thus leading to a very modest year-to-date performance of just under 4%. Fundamentally, the chipmaker — which is heavily exposed to the Chinese auto market — may be facing broader economic challenges. Still, the weakness could offer a contrarian opportunity for bold speculators.

On paper, circumstances would seem optimistic. In the company's second-quarter earnings report, it exceeded headline metrics. According to Google Finance's summary sheet, NXP reported record non-GAAP earnings of $3.61 per share and revenue of approximately $3.50 billion, thus resulting in 19.5% growth year-over-year. Contributing to the strong print were accelerating adoption of software-defined vehicles and expanding physical AI infrastructure applications.

More News from Barchart

Option Volatility and Earnings Report For Aug 24-28

Markets move fast. Keep up by reading our FREE midday Barchart Brief newsletter for exclusive charts, analysis, and headlines.

Unfortunately, the market was skeptical about the future trajectory of NXPI stock, especially due to auto industry concerns. Analysts raised alarm about global inventory risks stemming from a potential slowdown in China, along with other macroeconomic headwinds. Such anxieties aren't exclusive to NXP, with the wider chip industry experiencing selling pressure.

At the same time, the counterbalancing argument is that China is aggressively transitioning to electric vehicles. This macro tailwind should help lift NXP's semiconductor value per car significantly. Therefore, it's not a foregone conclusion that NXPI stock will be permanently stuck with a technical sell rating.

What's more, the current quantitative structure of NXPI is quite unique. In the last 10 weekly sessions, the ticker has only managed to print two positive candlesticks, leading to an overall downward slope. Under this 2-8-D quantitative sequence (2 up, 8 down, downward slope), the market tends to generate a positive forward bias for NXPI stock.

How much of a bias? Well, there's an inductive reason why I'm looking at the 250/260 bull call spread expiring Oct. 16.

Multiple Presuppositions Battle for NXPI Stock

Story Continues

To be fair, when you look at the forecasted stats for the 250/260 call spread, they don't exactly inspire confidence. For one thing, you would need serious juice for NXPI stock to rise about 15.3% from Friday's close to trigger the second-leg strike price, which would result in a 104.08% maximum payout. However, the current implied volatility (IV) for the Oct. 16 options chain is 42.67%, whereas the historic volatility for the period is 43.61%.

Why is that a problem? IV metrics stem from actual orders. Therefore, if market participants' various transactions imply less-than-historical expectations for share price movement, expecting a move of over 15% over the next eight weeks seems extremely (perhaps unreasonably) optimistic.

In fact, this is a big reason why the probability of profit is listed at 23%. Nominally, there's a very low chance that NXPI stock will hit $254.90 at expiration, let alone the $260 strike. And what about the strike? If you reverse engineer Barchart's Expected Move calculator, you're looking at a probability of only 18.93%.

So the conclusion is rather obvious: if we were to accept the above odds as absolute truth, then the NXPI stock call spread would be completely reckless. The question, though, is whether or not the odds provided are indeed absolute truth?

Here's the harsh reality: from an epistemological framework, we can know absolutely nothing about the unknown future. Even concepts like "before and "after" are presuppositional. Just because these concepts existed throughout deep time does not necessarily mean we can rely on them with absolute certainty.

Now, I'm not going to suggest that "tomorrow" will not come. From a more practical view, at the heart of the above probabilities is the concept of the random walk. For example, the idea that NXPI stock hitting $260 on Oct. 16 representing only an 18.93% chance didn't come out of nowhere. Instead, these are the legitimate odds if, given the initial IV, NXPI incurred Brownian motion (i.e. random trading dynamics) from now until expiration.

My presupposition, though, is that because NXPI stock suffers from a sharply negative order flow balance, it will likely incur a nonrandom journey. Under this framework, I believe the odds — while not particularly "good" — are higher than what would be assumed under random conditions.

Detailing the Inductive Math Behind NXP Semiconductor Stock

The question now becomes, why did I specifically look at the 250/260 bull spread expiring Oct. 16? Essentially, of the rare few times that we've seen the 2-8-D quant sequence flash since January 2019, NXP Semiconductor stock has delivered an impressive upside performance.

By the raw count, the above signal has flashed 12 times on a rolling basis. Of this figure, NXPI stock has exceeded the equivalent of the $260 strike a total of six times at the end of the eighth week (Oct. 16) following the signal materializing on the charts. Granted, we're talking about an extremely small sample size but so far, the observed condition probability of full profitability is 50%.

In other words, if we gamble that this bullish trend were to repeat in the future, the median endpoint expectation on Oct. 16 is a price of around $260. If so, that may be enough to trigger the second-leg strike, thus resulting in a robust payout.

It must be acknowledged, though, that this framework is a matter of inference, not logical necessity. There's no guarantee that NXP Semiconductor stock will reach $260 at expiration. Also, since we're dealing with a limited sample size, it's not possible to have high statistical confidence.

At the same time, I'm not entirely convinced that NXPI stock will undergo a random walk into October. Because the order flow balance is so negative, I'm betting on major players looking at the quantitative weakness of NXPI as a discounted opportunity.

news.Title: Arm Holdings (ARM) Delivers Strong Growth, but Has the Valuation Run Too Far?
news.Content:
Sustainable Growth Advisers  (SGA), an investment management company, released its second-quarter 2026 investor letter for its "Global Growth Strategy." The letter can be downloaded here . The SGA Global Growth Portfolio returned 7.4% gross and 7.2% net, compared with 14.9% for the MSCI ACWI and 19.8% for the MSCI ACWI Growth Index. Momentum leadership and enthusiasm around AI infrastructure drove markets, with semiconductor, memory, and hardware stocks accounting for much of the gain. Although the portfolio owned AI beneficiaries, broader holdings lagged despite fundamentals, as median revenue and EPS growth reached 12% and 14% and more than 60% of the holdings beat expectations. SGA believes valuation compression reflects sentiment rather than weaker business quality, leaving the portfolio near its widest discount to the market since inception. The firm continues to favor durable compounders and expects 16% revenue growth and 20% earnings growth over three years. Management guidance reinforced confidence in maintaining roughly 20% revenue growth, supported by increasing demand for Arm-based CPUs and expanding adoption across data center and AI workloads, which helped offset expected weakness in handset markets. Confidence was further supported by evidence of strong CPU demand, improving share gains versus x86 architectures, and growing customer traction, including an expanding roster of signed partners and management's confidence in achieving long-term revenue targets. With strong pricing power, highly recurring revenues, and expanding royalty rates as Arm captures more value across the compute stack, we continue to view the company as a high-quality, long-term compounder well-positioned to benefit from the proliferation of AI and power efficient computing.
